acceptance_test_interpretation: AT01 establishes that the generated paired worlds require cross-episode lifetime information under six actions and reject target-only/current-state/identifier/passive/action-string shortcuts; its no-memory upper bound must be a frozen, genuinely adaptive controller. AT02 makes positive memory atomic, one-edge, target-independent, provenance-valid, chronological, and insulated from workspace/terminal-branch laundering. AT03 makes every checkpoint a causal prefix and every arm a read-only common-deck recipient. AT04 separates a copy ceiling, atomic-memory read ceiling, non-adaptive retrieval ceiling, recurrent construction, and proof completion before learned transport. AT05 permits jointly sufficient atomic premises only through adaptive legal reads and requires a dependency DAG, while forbidding an individual record or return from storing a solution. AT06 measures sequential action, public-outcome-conditioned revision, and every cognitive/action stage separately; correct uncited action is not composition evidence. AT07 tests the supported text pipeline against no memory, raw episodic/RAG, and independently organized text with equal controller/read/action resources and a matched outcome shuffle. AT08 asks whether the exact E-text corpus retains action value after per-life LoRA transport and beats direct-QA and external-memory controls without deleting failed capped cells. AT09 closes target-goal/query/candidate, backend, cache, scorer, cross-item, and cross-life channels. AT10 requires the presently absent exact executable bundle and fresh deliberation before implementation. AT11 is the only claim-eligible post-context confirmation, clustered by twin-pair and using preregistered paired uncertainty. AT12 independently verifies every pre-GPU gate and cannot be overridden by the author-side advocate.

ambiguities.question: The proposal deliberately defers exact generator/world/target manifests, canonical goal and public-state bytes, prompts, parsers, reader/candidate implementation, model revisions, adaptive controller, independent builder, resource ledger, seed/failure rules, and estimator implementation to AT10. These choices can materially alter necessity, reader fidelity, and measured effects; they require a new bound bundle and human ratification rather than implementation inference.

Fixed-memory comparison is not yet operationally defined across text, RAG, explicit graph-like organized memory, and LoRA: active bytes, retained source/corpus bytes, candidate-universe size, index state, reader computation, and model-input tokens need a single bound accounting rule. Equal query and operation counts alone do not prevent text search or candidate recognition from giving one substrate more effective access.

AT01 names Bayes-optimal and frozen 32B no-lifetime-memory controls but does not yet bind their observations, algorithms/prompts, internal scratch, information-gathering strategy, tie-breaking, development selection, and per-family threshold calculation. Without this, a weak control can make memory appear necessary, while an untested standard agent/raw context/RAG/answer-prior route can bypass the intended path.

The calibration evaluates 0.5C, 1C, and 2C for causal isolation but locks model results at 2C; AT11 later adds 0..16C. The proposal describes recurrent sleep but does not include a matched batch/bridge-removal cadence contrast in the named initial causal contrasts. Thus it can test prefix-causal accumulation and length effects only after the exact bundle specifies checkpoints and cannot support recurrent-sleep superiority in this change.

Normalized A2/A3 value, 'materially improves,' action regret, exact half-gain removal, the four-of-six rule, fixed-query read fidelity, and treatment of malformed/infrastructure versus scientific failures need executable formulas. They must also bind target weighting, twin aggregation, adapter-seed handling, and whether every action-success without proof remains a composition failure in all aggregate reports.

assumptions: The supplied proposal hash and each supplied context-file hash are authoritative for this interpretation.

A local reader return is immutable and can expose at most one atomic ontology edge plus non-answer-bearing provenance handles; it cannot indirectly encode omitted candidate scores, rank, backend identity, or target-specific retrieval behavior.
Fresh handles and paired-world marginal matching are generated independently of all cognition, and the hidden oracle is unavailable to every cognitive process.
The frozen resolver may use pretrained priors only through declared prompts and public current state; such priors are not treated as lifetime memory evidence.

All claims of accumulation concern supported atoms across source prefixes and dreams within a life; goal-conditioned multi-edge paths are constructed transiently in the wake workspace and are not written back during sealed evaluation.
The fixed-deck assay identifies memory representation/use under common experience, not policy-selected evidence acquisition, online updating from evaluation, or a continual flywheel.
claim_delta_interpretation: C1 can be supported only as a descriptive, locked-ledger bundled-pipeline result: authentic, supported experience-derived memory plus the common reader and frozen recurrent resolver improves held-out A2/A3 action over its named controls. It does not identify DREAM, compiler, reader, resolver, or LoRA individually. C2 additionally requires AT11 confirmation and supports only near-text per-life parametric transport at post-context checkpoints against D-LoRA and A-text; it does not show LoRA sufficiency or discovery. C3 correctly preserves failed cells and makes oracle/text failure a stop before transport, while transport failure leaves a benchmark/compiler result at most. C4 forbids claims of learned THINK/DREAM, recurrent-sleep superiority, online reconsolidation, action-selected evidence, continued improvement, beyond-context scaling absent the specified confirmation, external validity, or general intelligence.

context_files.purpose: Developmental protocol lineage and visibility contract

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: AT10's exact bundle must explicitly include no-memory standard-agent, within-C raw-context, strongest pinned native-long-context where applicable, raw episodic RAG, independent organized text/graph-interface, direct-QA LoRA, target-only and answer-prior probes under one visibility/resource ledger.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The named AT07 arms are valuable but do not by themselves bind the full range of standard-agent, raw-context, explicit-graph, candidate-recognition, and answer-prior bypasses emphasized by the project thesis. A fair common reader cannot be assumed from a common output schema.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposal treats its named text suite and visibility assertions as adequate evidence against all bypass paths.

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Register a matched batch-at-L versus recurrent-prefix comparison, bridge-removal/shuffled-connectivity ablations, and exact life-length/scale checkpoints in the later execution bundle; report them as distinct tests, not as consequences of E-LoRA success.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: AT03 establishes prefix noninterference and AT11 contains later checkpoint scaling, but neither initial calibration contrast estimates whether intermediate dreams or bridge connectivity, rather than total evidence/corpus size, cause improvement. C4 appropriately forbids a recurrence claim until then.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The architecture's recurrent sleep loop may be read as though a passed bundled pipeline demonstrates benefit from recurrence or local bridge accumulation.

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Predeclare a substrate-neutral capacity ledger covering corpus/index/adapter bytes, reader-visible tokens, candidate-universe enumeration, retrieval/index compute, reader inference compute, training tokens/FLOPs, and query/action budgets; report native explicit-graph performance separately from the common interface.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: Text can retrieve explicit records while LoRA must perform candidate recognition, so equal source life, query count, and controller budget do not by themselves establish a fixed-memory substrate comparison. The project context explicitly warns that the resolution protocol can carry the intelligence.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposal's equal-budget language is sufficient to make E-text and E-LoRA a fixed-memory comparison.

graph_delta_interpretation: The proposed organism is: a fixed ordinary source life creates public action/outcome roots; DREAM adds target-independent, one-edge, falsifiable proposals; only later ordinary source evidence assigns support; SLEEP compiles supported atoms into text or rebuilds a clean-base per-life LoRA; a common reader exposes one typed local return; a frozen wake resolver adaptively joins local dependencies into a temporary goal-conditioned path, executes typed actions sequentially, and uses only current-item public outcomes to revise. Evaluation is read-only and scorer truth is offline. This correctly places durable growth in local supported memory and transient composition in the thinker, but its causal force depends on AT02/03/05/06/09 being mechanically implemented rather than narrative declarations.

open_questions: Whether Rohin will ratify a new exact execution bundle resolving A01-A05 and the stated scope; no present agreement authorizes implementation or a run.
Which exact resource-accounting rule defines fair fixed-memory text, RAG, graph-like, and LoRA comparisons.
Whether recurrence/bridge and lifetime-scale ablations belong in the first bound bundle or remain explicitly deferred without causal or headline attribution.
Which frozen adaptive no-lifetime-memory controller and standard-agent/raw-context baselines establish necessity without target leakage.

loop_delta_interpretation: L1 is a causal prefix loop: proposal at or before a checkpoint, later-source confirmation or contradiction, supported-only compilation, and cumulative clean-base rebuild. Its temporal order prevents terminal claims at 2C entering positive data and allows local edges from multiple dreams to accumulate only through ordinary source evidence. L2 is intentionally not a memory-growth loop: at most four adaptive reads and eight operations construct a path when a fresh goal arrives, then each of up to six actions yields a public current-item outcome that can cause revision but cannot write lifetime memory. L3 is only an architectural placeholder for the full action-to-dream-to-memory-to-later-action flywheel and supplies no evidence in this assay.
system_thesis_interpretation: The full organism seeks a continual causal flywheel, but this first assay isolates a narrow middle arrow: common lived action-outcome experience becomes provenance-supported local structure, then a bounded substrate plus frozen recurrent resolution improves novel action. Its core benchmark requirement is constructive necessity: paired worlds must make lifetime-specific bindings indispensable, no record or one read may copy an A2/A3 answer, non-adaptive access must fail, and adaptive joins across separately acquired atoms must produce an auditable proof and sequential action. It measures memory transport and bounded composition before, not instead of, later tests of action-selected evidence and continued improvement.
visibility_matrix_interpretation: The matrix provides the correct temporal firewall: source prefixes feed dream/compiler only at the appropriate checkpoint; suffixes are forbidden; goals are visible only to the evaluation resolver; current-item outcomes permit within-item revision only; semantic lifecycle, hidden truth, and scorer/audit state are excluded from cognition; evaluation cannot alter source life. Benchmark validity still requires process-level noninterference over every model-visible byte—goal canonicalization, candidate universe/order, query arguments/timing, reader returns, cache keys, backend failure modes, training examples, and cross-item state—because a declared forbidden field can otherwise reappear as a target-only shortcut or substrate-identity channel.
